title: Shader Energy Transfer Console
description: A BoomBox and InterpolationTest model are connected by animated energy beams rendered with custom shaders. The user manipulates shader parameters (hue, distortion, glow intensity, fresnel power, dissolve threshold) across both models, transferring a fixed 'energy budget' between them. An undo/redo system tracks every parameter change, and coupled inputs ensure total energy is always conserved.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads BoomBox.glb (scaled up 200x, positioned at x=-2) and InterpolationTest.glb (positioned at x=2). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0,2,6) looking at origin, with OrbitControls, ambient light (0.3), and two directional lights. Apply custom ShaderMaterial overrides to every mesh of both models. The vertex shader should include a uniform-driven sine-wave vertex distortion and a fresnel term passed to the fragment shader. The fragment shader should combine the original texture (sampled via a tDiffuse uniform) with: (1) hue-shift via HSL rotation, (2) glow rim using fresnel, (3) dissolve effect using a noise threshold that discards fragments. Create a right-side HTML panel with these controls per model (10 total sliders): hue shift 0-360, vertex distortion amplitude 0-1, glow intensity 0-2, fresnel power 0.5-5, dissolve threshold 0-1. Implement an energy conservation system: a global budget of 5.0 is split between models. Each model's 'energy' equals the sum of its normalized slider values. When any slider changes, auto-adjust the OTHER model's glow intensity slider to maintain the total at exactly 5.0, clamping if needed. Display both energy values and the total in the panel. Draw a custom shader-based beam (a cylinder geometry between the two models) whose color and pulsation speed reflect the energy differential. Implement undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y that stores full snapshots of all 10 slider values; support at least 50 history states. Show undo/redo buttons in the panel. Update all shader uniforms every frame via requestAnimationFrame. The interaction requires 10-14 steps: adjusting sliders on both models, observing coupled changes, using undo/redo to revert states, and verifying conservation holds.
